reason: The cited evidence does not directly test or report on CoCrFeNi+WC composite coatings. E2 mentions a different HEA (FeCoNiCrMo0.2) with WC on 316L, providing partial support for the concept, but the specific matrix, substrate, and synergistic corrosion-wear mechanism are not evidenced. E1, E3, and E4 offer only general background on HEAs, corrosion, and laser cladding, leaving key premises largely unsupported by specific prior results.
premises: CoCrFeNi HEA provides a tough matrix with good bonding and refined microstructure via laser cladding
WC particles reinforce hardness and inhibit crack propagation in the cladding layer
Laser cladding produces dense, metallurgically bonded coatings with low dilution and rapid solidification
The composite coating improves wear and corrosion resistance over untreated or fusion-welded surfaces
